## Summary

Under an EBA-based adverse scenario the 12-month bankruptcy rate across nine industries peaks
at **0.95 per 100 firms** in 2027Q4 (80 % interval
0.85–1.06), against 0.72 in
the latest four quarters. In Konjunkturinstitutet's baseline the rate eases to
0.60. A 1 percentage-point rise in unemployment over a year is associated with a
+11.6 % change in expected bankruptcies (95 % CI +6.5 to +16.9 %).

![](figures/hero.png)

The model does not beat a seasonal-naive forecast one year ahead in the untouched test period
(MAE 0.171 vs 0.100 pp), and its 80 % intervals covered only
38 % of outcomes. The scenario paths should be read as directional.

## Data and validation

Bankruptcies come from Tillväxtanalys (monthly by industry, 2009 onwards, one table), firms
from SCB's Business Register (FDB, November stock), unemployment and GDP from SCB, and the
policy rate from the Riksbank. The rate is bankruptcies per quarter × 4 divided by the
previous November's stock. With this denominator our 2023 rates reproduce all nine shares
published by Tillväxtanalys after rounding (mean absolute deviation 0.030 pp).
The nine industries plus "unspecified" add up exactly to the independent county total in
every month.

## Model

Negative binomial (NB2) regression of quarterly counts with log(firms) as offset, industry
fixed effects, quarterly seasonality, a trend, a pandemic-support dummy (2020Q2–2021Q4,
-26.0 %, CI -33.4 to -17.7 %) and three macro drivers. Poisson
is clearly overdispersed (Pearson χ²/df 5.05; NB2: 1.11).

| Driver (same quarter) | Effect on bankruptcies | 95 % CI |
|---|---|---|
| Unemployment, +1 pp y/y | +11.6 % | +6.5 to +16.9 % |
| GDP growth, +1 % y/y | +0.5 % | -0.7 to +1.7 % |
| Policy rate, +1 pp y/y | +0.9 % | -1.7 to +3.5 % |

The specification grid (8 models), the selection metric (firm-weighted MAE at four quarters)
and the watchlist rule were committed before estimation. Selected: `A_k0`.

![](figures/model_residual_diagnostics.png)

## Backtest

![](figures/backtest_mae.png)

| h = 4, MAE (pp of annual rate) | Selection period | Test period |
|---|---|---|
| Satellite | 0.082 | 0.171 |
| Seasonal naive | 0.073 | 0.100 |
| ETS | 0.075 | 0.108 |
| NB2 without macro | 0.082 | 0.182 |

The backtest is conditional on actual macro outcomes. With KI's real-time forecast vintages
the test-period MAE is 0.184.

## Scenarios

![](figures/scenario_macro_paths.png)

![](figures/scenario_fans_by_sector.png)

| Industry | Rate now | Adverse peak (80 % interval) | Window |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hotels and restaurants | 2.50 | 3.06 (2.63–3.55) | 2027Q1–2027Q4 |
| Construction | 1.56 | 2.07 (1.79–2.38) | 2027Q1–2027Q4 |
| Trade | 1.53 | 2.07 (1.79–2.38) | 2027Q1–2027Q4 |
| Transport | 1.52 | 1.93 (1.66–2.24) | 2027Q1–2027Q4 |
| Manufacturing | 0.75 | 1.22 (1.05–1.42) | 2027Q1–2027Q4 |
| Information and communication | 0.73 | 0.84 (0.72–0.97) | 2027Q1–2027Q4 |
| Finance, real estate, business services | 0.55 | 0.75 (0.65–0.86) | 2027Q1–2027Q4 |
| Education, health, other services | 0.40 | 0.45 (0.39–0.52) | 2027Q1–2027Q4 |

Rates are bankruptcies per 100 firms per year (rolling four quarters for "now", the
four-quarter window average for the peak). Reverse stress test: unemployment would have to
rise by 6.3 pp within a year (80 % interval 5.0–8.7)
to double the bankruptcy rate; with the common slope this threshold is the same for every
industry.

## Bank perspective (synthetic portfolio)

![](figures/pd_overlay_by_sector.png)

The PD overlay is the scenario rate relative to the industry's historical mean and uses only
real data. On a **synthetic** 5,000-loan SME portfolio (LGD 45 %, weights 70/30), the
probability-weighted 12-month ECL is +17 % above the
through-the-cycle ECL. This is a simplification of IFRS 9: no staging, no SICR, no lifetime PD.

## Monitoring

Each new complete quarter is compared with the model's previous forecast: green inside the
80 % interval, yellow outside once, red outside two quarters in a row (re-estimation
trigger). Latest quarter (2026Q2): 6 green,
1 yellow, 2 red.

## Limitations

Bankruptcy is a late and narrow proxy for default; FDB includes dormant firms; few cycles;
the pandemic break; the common slope; y/y drivers that fade once unemployment stops rising;
no scenario probabilities; a simplified ECL on synthetic loans. See the README and
`docs/decisions.md`.

*Sources: Tillväxtanalys, SCB, Sveriges riksbank, Konjunkturinstitutet, EBA/ESRB. Own
calculations.*
